title: Choose the safe response to release evidence
description: Inject an artifact or data condition, then choose how the release should proceed. The path shows which evidence remains trustworthy and where promotion must stop.

stages.label: Input contract
stages.detail: Names, types, missing-value policy, and request availability match the candidate.

stages.label: Preprocessing
stages.detail: The serving path loads the vocabulary, normalizer, and category metadata produced during training.

stages.label: Evaluation
stages.detail: Held-out metrics, slice checks, and threshold behavior meet the release policy.

stages.label: Serving canary
stages.detail: Representative requests pass schema, latency, and prediction smoke tests.

actions.label: Release all traffic
actions.detail: Replace the current version immediately without a guarded observation window.

actions.label: Canary the candidate
actions.detail: Send a bounded traffic slice, compare service and model metrics, then promote deliberately.

actions.label: Shadow and investigate
actions.detail: Run the candidate without affecting user decisions while collecting representative evidence.

actions.label: Block or roll back
actions.detail: Keep the last known-good artifact active and repair the candidate before retrying.

conditions.label: All release evidence passes
conditions.detail: The candidate uses the versioned config and preprocessing metadata, passes held-out slice gates, and clears request smoke tests.
conditions.impact: The candidate is eligible for bounded exposure, but offline evidence still does not justify an unobserved full rollout.
conditions.reason: A canary limits blast radius and verifies latency, request validity, and live data behavior before broad promotion.

conditions.label: A required feature disappears
conditions.detail: The live producer stopped sending product_area, while the candidate still declares it as an input feature.
conditions.impact: Requests will fail validation or silently receive an unreviewed missing-value treatment.
conditions.reason: Block promotion until the producer and model contract agree; do not use rollout traffic to discover a known schema break.

conditions.label: Unknown categories rise sharply
conditions.detail: A new product launch sends category values that were rare or absent in the training metadata.
conditions.impact: The request schema is valid, but production representation and slice quality are uncertain.
conditions.reason: Shadow traffic reveals unknown-category rates and prediction behavior without making the candidate authoritative.

conditions.label: Model and preprocessing metadata diverge
conditions.detail: The container includes the candidate weights but loads category metadata from the previous run.
conditions.impact: Input values can map to different tensors than the model saw during training, invalidating offline evidence.
conditions.reason: Weights and preprocessing metadata form one release artifact. Restore the last coherent bundle and rebuild the candidate.

notice: The scenarios model release decisions. Set thresholds from measured service-level objectives, slice performance, and business cost; do not copy generic pass values into production.
